title: Job 902117 checkpoint throughput degradation and its evidence limits
difficulty_justification: A job-record lookup must be converted into an explicitly documented machine-readable answer: independently compute two complementary throughput percentages, keep CPU efficiency and frequency loss distinct, recognise missing per-variant evidence and reported rather than demonstrated causality, and choose a researcher-safe escalation. Exact output conventions are visible in the query; there is no hidden formatting requirement.
query_text:
I am carol, the researcher who owns climate-lab job 902117. Read its cluster record and report checkpoint throughput, the distinct CPU/thermal figures, whether the slowest of the 16 ensemble variants is identifiable, and the appropriate role-safe next step. Do not treat a recorded attribution as independently established causality.
Return ONLY one semicolon-separated line, in exactly this field order, with no spaces:
job_id=<id>;observed_mbps=<number>;expected_mbps=<number>;remaining_pct=<number>;reduction_pct=<number>;cpu_efficiency_pct=<number>;cpu_frequency_reduction_pct=<number>;inlet_c=<number>;slowest_variant=<value>;cause=<value>;next_action=<value>
Use integers without .0; otherwise use the shortest exact decimal (e.g. 2.5). Percentages are in percent units, not fractions. For slowest_variant use its name only if the snapshot contains enough per-variant measurements; otherwise use not_identifiable. cause must be reported_attribution, independently_established, or unknown. next_action must be escalate_to_ops, modify_cooling_directly, or no_action. Choose based on the evidence and researcher permissions. Obtain evidence with allowed tools; do not guess unavailable measurements.
